ropeway:tower-incomplete: Tower is not complete, {0} blocks missing or wrong.
ropeway:cell-any: Post block - log, planks or dressed stone
ropeway:blockinfo-passage: The cabin will pass through {0} to {1}
ropeway:blockinfo-machineleg: The machine leg goes on the {0} side. To put it {1} instead, break this footing and place it again standing on the other side of it - the cabin still passes the same way.
ropeway:sheave-attached: Sheave of the tower whose footing is four blocks below.
ropeway:sheave-orphan: Not part of a tower. A tower starts with a pylon footing on the ground; the sheave goes on top of its crossarm.
ropeway:blockinfo-endpoint: End of line - rides turn around here
ropeway:blockinfo-line-truncated: Part of this line is in unloaded chunks. The cabin stops at the last loaded tower.
ropeway:bullwheel-what: The big wheel of the station whose footing is four blocks below - the driving wheel on a drive station, the return wheel the counterweight pulls on a tension station. At the end of a line the haul rope wraps half way round it, arriving on the lower strand and leaving on the upper one a wheel's diameter higher, which is what makes the rope a loop. Its hub axle runs out along the crossarm to the machinery, and it turns whenever the line's drive is running.
ropeway:bullwheel-orphan: Not part of a station. A bullwheel goes in the middle of a drive station's or a tension station's crossarm, four blocks above its footing.
ropeway:shaftsheave-what: The winding wheel of the shaft whose head footing is four blocks below. The haul rope comes up the shaft from the car, goes half way round it and comes back down the counterweight's lane three blocks along - so the two hang on one rope and the drive lifts only the difference. Its hub axle runs out to the lay shaft beside it, and it turns whenever the shaft's drive is running.
ropeway:shaftsheave-orphan: Not part of a shaft. A shaft sheave goes four blocks directly above a shaft head footing.
ropeway:housing-what: The mechanical intake at the foot of a drive station's leg. Run an axle into any of its four sides; the drive shafts above it carry the power up to the bullwheel.
ropeway:blockinfo-nodrive: No mechanical power here. An axle may enter from any of the four sides.
ropeway:blockinfo-linedrive: The line's drives move the cabin at {0} blocks a second.
ropeway:blockinfo-nolinedrive: Nothing on this line is turning, so the cabin will not move. One of its towers has to be a drive station with an axle run into the housing at the foot of its leg. It need not be finished - a drive station missing a brace still drives.
ropeway:blockinfo-notensioner: This line has no tension station. One of its towers has to be a finished tension station before it will carry a cabin.
ropeway:err-no-tensioner: This line has no tension station to keep the rope taut. Build one of its towers as a tension station and finish it first.
ropeway:blockinfo-cabin-here: The cabin is at this tower.
ropeway:blockinfo-cabin-coming: The cabin is on its way here.
ropeway:blockinfo-cabin-elsewhere: The cabin is elsewhere on the line.
ropeway:err-tower-full: That tower already carries two spans.
ropeway:err-not-linked: Those towers are not linked to each other.
ropeway:err-self-link: You cannot link a tower to itself.
ropeway:err-span-too-long: Span too long. Maximum is {0} blocks.
ropeway:err-span-blocked: The span is blocked. The rope and the cabin need a clear corridor three wide, from the return strand overhead down past the cabin's floor.
ropeway:err-line-too-long: Line too long. Maximum is {0} blocks.
ropeway:err-not-enough-rope: Not enough haul rope. Need {0}, you have {1}.
ropeway:err-too-far: You are too far from that tower.
ropeway:err-cabin-exists: This line already has a cabin.
ropeway:err-not-endpoint: The cabin can only be placed at an end tower.
ropeway:err-cabin-here: The cabin is already at this tower.
ropeway:err-no-drive: Nothing on this line is turning, so the cabin cannot set off. Wait for the wind and ask again, or make one of this line's towers a drive station and run a mill into it.
ropeway:err-line-truncated: Part of this line is in unloaded chunks. The cabin waits at the last loaded tower until they load.
ropeway:err-line-truncated-link: Part of that line is in unloaded chunks, so it cannot be measured. Get closer to the rest of it first.
ropeway:err-shaft-column: A shaft runs straight up one column, from a shaft foot to a shaft head above it, and both footings must face the same way - the foot's facing is where you dug the counterweight's guide and the head's is where the counterweight comes down. A shaft station links only to the other end of its own shaft, and never to a ropeway tower.
ropeway:err-shaft-one-span: A shaft footing carries one span. There are no intermediate floors yet: one foot, one head, one car.
ropeway:span-linked: Span strung to {0}: {1} blocks, {2} haul rope.
ropeway:span-cut: Span to {0} cut. {1} haul rope recovered.
ropeway:corner-facing: {0} now turns the line {1} degrees, and its crossarm points the wrong way for that. Break the footing and re-place it facing {2}, or the cabin will clip a post going through.
ropeway:corner-too-sharp: {0} now turns the line {1} degrees, which is sharper than any of the four tower facings can carry - the cabin will clip a post going through. The line still works; a gentler corner or an extra tower is the cure.
ropeway:span-too-steep: That span climbs at {0} degrees. A tower can pass the cabin cleanly up to about {1}: steeper than that, the cabin's roof passes through the crossarm as it leaves the lower tower, and its floor through the footing as it comes down into one. The line still works and still carries riders - a gentler span, or another tower part way up the slope, is the only cure.
ropeway:cabin-held-truncated: The line carries on into unloaded chunks. Holding at this tower.
ropeway:call-abandoned-blocked: The cabin you called stopped on the way: the span ahead of it is blocked.
ropeway:call-abandoned-truncated: The cabin you called stopped at the last loaded tower: part of the line is in unloaded chunks.
ropeway:call-abandoned-line: The cabin you called stopped on the way: the line changed under it.
ropeway:cantride-moving: The cabin is moving. Wait until it stops at a tower.
ropeway:cantunmount-moving: The cabin is moving. Wait until it stops at a tower - or hold {0} for {1} seconds to jump out, and take the fall.
ropeway:cantunmount-noground: Nothing under the cabin but air. It carries on to a tower by itself once the line turns again - then hold {0} for {1} seconds if you would rather jump, and take the fall.
ropeway:bailed-out: You jumped out of the cabin between {0} and {1}. It carries on without you.
ropeway:ride-hint: Ropeway: press {0} to get off at the next tower. Press again for the one after it, and keep going past the end of the line to come back the other way.
ropeway:ridecam-hint: Ropeway: press {0} for an outside view of the cabin, and again to come back inside.
ropeway:err-no-stop: No stop to ask for from here.
ropeway:dlg-picker-row-linked: Connected: {0} - {1} blocks - click to cut (+{2} rope)
ropeway:dlg-picker-empty: No connections, and no linkable towers in range.
ropeway:dlg-guide-body: A tower is 16 blocks: the pylon footing you already placed, plus 15 more. One crossarm on two legs - it is a doorway, not a tunnel. 1. Two posts of four blocks each, standing on the ground three blocks either side of the footing - logs, debarked logs, planks, raw stone, cobblestone, drystone, polished rock or stone bricks, whichever suits what you build in. 2. A seven-wide crossarm across their tops: the pylon head in the middle, directly four above the footing, and three ropeway braces either side of it. The head carries a short mast with a saddle on top, above the sheave: the haul rope is a loop, and that saddle is what its return strand rides on as it comes back overhead. That leaves a clear 5 wide, 4 tall archway, and the cabin passes through it along the axis the footing's block info panel names - so face the footing down the line before you build. On a tower that turns the line, face it down the halfway line between its two spans rather than down either one: the path itself curves through a corner tower, and the cabin, the drawn rope and the station rails all sweep onto that halfway line together. Linking the second span tells you in chat if the crossarm points the wrong way for the corner it just made. Right-click the footing and the rest of the tower appears around it: every empty cell grows a see-through copy of the block that goes in it, and the footing's own panel lists them with their counts. A post cell gets a plain coloured box rather than a ghost, because what goes in one is your choice of material; a cell holding the wrong block is lit red. Making it move: a line needs two of its towers built as stations rather than plain towers. A station is the same sixteen cells in the same footprint - one leg of it is machinery instead of posts, and that is the only difference. Place a drive station footing at the end nearest your mill and a tension station footing at the far end, and face each down the line exactly as you would a plain footing. Both stations take the same crossarm: three ropeway braces on the plain side, a bullwheel in the middle instead of the pylon head, then two lay shafts running out to the machine leg. The drive station's leg is a drive housing on the ground, three drive shafts above it and a drive head on the crossarm end. The tension station's is a tension weight on the ground, three tension guides above it and a tension head on the crossarm end. Right-click either footing and every cell it is still short of stands there as a see-through copy of the block that belongs in it. Then run an axle into any of the drive housing's four sides. The drive shafts are the one part of a tower an axle may lean on, so a mill on a ridge comes down the outside of the leg on ordinary wooden axles and angled gears. One drive station anywhere on a line drives all of it, and a second on its own axle network makes the cabin faster. The bullwheels turn whenever the line is running, so you can see from across the valley that the drive is working, and at the end of a line the rope wraps half way round one - in low, round, out high - which is what closes the loop. A line whose end towers are plain instead just runs its return strand onto the saddle on top of the tower and stops there, with no wheel to have turned it: it works, and it looks unfinished, because it is. The line will not take a cabin at all until one of its towers is a finished tension station. Riding: sit down and the cabin runs to the end of the line. Press {0} to get off at a tower in between - each press steps the selection one tower further along, and past the end of the line it comes back the other way. Press {1} for an outside view of the cabin while you ride, and again to come back inside. Both are listed in Settings > Controls if you would rather move them. Freight: Ctrl and right-click a bench holding a basket or a chest to load it onto that bench. Right-click a loaded bench to open it. A loaded bench cannot be sat on, so a cabin carries two loads, or one load and one passenger. Ctrl and right-click a bench with an empty hand to take the container off again - it has to be emptied first.
